- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) after a spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% in subsequent periods.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >80) by forecasting higher prices for 2–3 periods; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.6), model shows mean-reversion bias — forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average of prior 10 days.  
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a high, model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 period lag in price drop.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is weak or declining; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment < 0.4 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.3 → +0.6), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 sentiment values to adjust forecast direction.
